title: The People Process
coreMove: Make talent review answer the business plan instead of sitting beside it as a separate ritual.
sourcePressure: Core process one: the people process must link people to strategy and operations through pipeline depth, succession, retention risk, nonperformance, HR linkage, and candid dialogue.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Make this an HR process chapter about forms and annual reviews.

sourceAnchors.name: Honeywell talent review
sourceAnchors.detail: the source sidecar names Talent Review At Honeywell as a chapter heading but warns not to invent meeting choreography or process scenes beyond that heading
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A Honeywell talent review belongs as a reminder that people process is operating work, not as permission to invent a corporate ritual.

hook: the the people process that nobody sees until it is too late
a meeting room where every plan sounds good
a generic promise colliding with reality
counterintuition: Most leaders think X, but the opposite is true
The problem is not effort, it is discipline
Execution is not about working harder
tryThisNow: set a timer and write three priorities
audit one goal in your notebook
ask yourself what matters most today
examples: generic project kickoff with vague owners
student team with a deadline and no specificity
family calendar scene used as a management analogy

exampleSpecs.domain: a hospital network preparing to open a rural oncology clinic with no second trained nurse lead
exampleSpecs.stakes: the clinic opening depends on succession depth that does not exist yet
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Olivia places the nurse-lead pipeline sheet beside the clinic launch plan so the people gap becomes a strategy risk
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The oncology clinic floor plan is complete, but the nurse-lead pipeline sheet has one name and no backup.

exampleSpecs.domain: a national parks maintenance division facing retirements before wildfire season
exampleSpecs.stakes: critical trail and pump expertise can leave before the operations plan begins
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Luke traces last season's breakdown to retention risk that was discussed after the vacancy instead of inside the people process
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Luke one closed trail and two retired pump mechanics to see the retention risk column was not decoration.

exampleSpecs.domain: a specialty insurer linking underwriter development to a new cyber-risk strategy
exampleSpecs.stakes: strategy growth fails if underwriters are not developed for the risk class
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Nicolas makes the talent review answer the cyber-risk strategy instead of describing people in isolation
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Which underwriter can price this risk in six months?" Nicolas asks before anyone opens the appraisal packet.

exampleSpecs.domain: a conservatory choosing replacements for two retiring accompanists before audition season
exampleSpecs.stakes: student auditions can collapse if succession depth is assumed rather than built
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sam predicts the first audition week failure and uses it to expose shallow succession depth
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What happens to an audition week when both accompanists retire in June?

exampleSpecs.domain: a regional food distributor carrying a nonperforming route supervisor through peak season
exampleSpecs.stakes: working around one weak performer hides damage in delivery accuracy and driver morale
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Kasia decides whether to keep routing around the supervisor or bring nonperformance into candid dialogue with business results attached
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 5:18 a.m., Kasia watches drivers rewrite a route sheet the supervisor approved the night before.

exampleSpecs.domain: a London architecture firm connecting HR data to delayed planning approvals
exampleSpecs.stakes: the firm keeps treating missed approvals as project problems when capability gaps are driving them
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Hadiya links HR capability notes to planning-approval delays and changes the review from descriptive to business-linked
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You see planning-approval delays in one file and Hadiya sees the same two capability notes in another.

skillTargets: link people process choices to live strategy and operations
spot shallow pipeline and succession depth before crisis
choose candid dialogue over descriptive talent labels

tryThisNowSpec: Put one critical role beside one live business goal and write the backup depth, retention risk, and development gap in one row.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
